description: God told Jeremiah to search Jerusalem for even one just and honest person, and He would spare the city. One faithful life carries more weight than we realize.
excerpt: This whole verse is God essentially saying, find one. Find one just and honest person in this whole city, and I will spare it. One. That is all He is asking for.
verse: "Run up and down every street in Jerusalem," says the Lord. "Look high and low; search throughout the city! If you can find even one just and honest person, I will not destroy the city."
body_html:
I love that God often lets us negotiate with Him.

This whole verse is God essentially saying, find one. Find one just and honest person in this whole city, and I will spare it. One. That is all He is asking for. Not a hundred. Not ten. One.

That kind of mercy shows up over and over in Scripture. Abraham did this exact same thing when God was about to destroy Sodom. He kept asking, what about fifty righteous? What about forty? What about thirty? All the way down to ten. And God kept saying yes. If there are ten, I will not destroy it.

He lets us come to Him. He lets us plead. He lets us bargain. He lets us stand in the gap for people and places we care about. And He listens. He responds. He engages with us.

That is not a distant God. That is a God who is deeply relational. Who invites us into what He is doing. Who wants to hear from us. Who is willing to hold off on judgment for the sake of even one faithful person.

It also makes me think about how much one person actually matters to God. Because if He would spare a whole city for one just person, then one person walking with Him is a bigger deal than we probably realize. That single life carries weight. That one person's faithfulness can hold back things we cannot see.

I want to be that one.

I want to be the kind of person whose life is so aligned with God that He would look at a whole city and say, because of her, I am going to hold back. I want to be salt and light in a way that actually matters. Not just for me. For the people around me. For the community I am in. For the place God has planted me.

We often underestimate the impact of one faithful life. But God does not.

And He is still looking. Still searching cities. Still counting the just and honest ones. Still willing to be moved by our prayers, our intercession, our willingness to stand in the gap.

Are you willing to be the one He is looking for in the place He has put you?
question: Are you willing to be the one He is looking for in the place He has put you?
